content.content: # Documentation Taskflow keeps three kinds of document under `docs/`. They do not carry equal weight. | Folder | What it is | Weight | |---|---|---| | `docs/adr/` | Architecture Decision Records: numbered, dated, reviewed. | **Authoritative.** | | `docs/product/` | Product notes written before or alongside a feature: intent, examples, wording. | Context only. | | `docs/support/` | Runbooks and support macros: what people observed. | Describes behaviour, never specifies it. | ## Precedence 1. An ADR is the specification for every question it addresses. The highest-numbered ADR that addresses a question is the one that applies; a later ADR supersedes an earlier one only where it says so. 2. Where a product note and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins. A product note that predates an ADR on the same subject is kept for history, not as a second opinion. 3. Support notes record what was seen at the time. They are never evidence of intended behaviour. 4. Code comments, `TODO`s and function names are not documentation. They are frequently stale. 5. Where no document speaks, the current behaviour of the code is authoritative, and a new feature follows the conventions of its sibling features (same error classes, same guards, same events). # Issue list — product notes _Written for the filter bar launch (2025-12). Kept for history; see `docs/adr/0009-issue-list-filters.md` for the current rules._ ## Filters The filter bar narrows the issue list and writes what it did into the URL, so a filtered list is a link you can send to a colleague. - **Status** — chips for the six statuses; several chips show issues in any of them. - **Assignee** — a member, or "Unassigned". The sidebar's "Assigned to me" entry just links to the list with the current user's id filled in. - **Labels** — pick several and the list shows issues that have any of them, exactly like status. - **Due before** — a timestamp; issues due at that instant or later are left out. The date picker sends midnight of the chosen day, so the chosen day itself is not shown. - **Show archived** — a toggle that mixes archived issues into the list. There is no archived-only view; people who need one use the export. The project page and the "My issues" page read the URL themselves; "My issues" shows the open statuses unless the URL names statuses. ## Counts The header count ("12 issues in Platform") is the number of rows the filter matches. # ADR 0009 — The issue list filter vocabulary - Status: accepted - Date: 2026-03-02 - Supersedes: the "Filters" section of `docs/product/issue-list-notes.md` where the two disagree. ## Context The issue list is filtered from the URL: the filter bar writes query parameters, the page reads them back, the Server Action and the export tooling send the same shape to the service, and the repository turns it into predicates. Three copies of "what does `status=…` mean" have grown apart. This record fixes one vocabulary and names the places that must agree on it. ## Decision 1. **One vocabulary, three places.** The URL codec (`parseIssueFilterParams` / `issueFilterToParams`), the filter schema that validates every server entry point, and the repository predicates accept the same values and give them the same meaning. A value the codec produces is a value the schema accepts and the repository understands. Pages do not parse the query string themselves. 2. **`assignee` / `author`.** A user id; for `assignee` also `none` (unassigned); for both also `me`, the signed-in user. `me` travels unchanged through the codec and the schema and is resolved by the service against the acting user, so an API caller and a page get the same answer. Omitting the parameter means "do not filter on it". 3. **`status`.** A comma list of statuses and/or the groups `open` and `closed`. `open` stands for every status that is not closed; `closed` for the closed statuses (the ones the project card and the digest already count as closed). A group expands to its members wherever it is read: the codec expands it when parsing, and the schema and the repository accept the group names as well, so `status=open` means the same on a page and in an API call. Unknown values are dropped by the codec and refused by the schema. 4. **`label`.** A comma list of label ids. An issue matches only when it carries **every** listed label (all-of). Any-of is what the status and priority lists do; labels are different because people narrow with them ("bug" and "regression"), they do not widen. 5. **`due_before`.** Either a calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` or a full ISO-8601 timestamp. - A calendar date is read in UTC and matches issues due at any time on that day **or earlier** — the whole day is included. - A full timestamp matches issues due strictly before that instant, as it always has. Issues without a due date never match. 6. **`archived`.** `1` includes archived issues alongside live ones; `only` lists archived issues and nothing else. Absent, the list shows live issues only. 7. **`priority`** is a comma list (any-of); **`q`** is a substring of the title or description; **`project`** narrows to one project. Unchanged. 8. **The reported `total` counts exactly the issues the filter matches**, at every entry point. ## Consequences - The "Assigned to me" sidebar link (`issues?assignee=me`) is a real filter, not a convention. - The "My issues" page's hard-coded list of open statuses becomes `status=open`. src/server/services/issue-service.ts:2: * Issue business rules: authorization, per-project issue quota, numbering, status transitions and the events every other concern reacts to. src/server/services/issue-service.ts:28: IssueFilterInput, src/server/services/issue-service.ts:126: if (before.status === input.status) return before; I’m aligning those paths and the sidebar link with the ADR.

content.text: The shared URL decoder is now used by both issue list pages, and the service resolves `me` against the acting user. The repository now handles status groups, unassigned explicitly, all-of labels, whole-day date bounds, and archived-only queries. I’m checking for type errors and missed filter entry points.
